The EPA established an actionable threshold of 1,000 particles per liter, with utilities required to issue public notification when concentrations exceed this limit. Systems serving between 3,300 and 10,000 residents must begin monitoring by January 2025, while smaller systems have until July 2025 to comply.

The agency based these standards on the 2023 National Microplastic Occurrence Study, which detected synthetic fibers and fragments in 87% of treated municipal water samples. EPA Administrator Michael Regan noted that the co-regulation of PFAS and microplastics addresses 'emerging contaminant clusters' that exhibit synergistic toxicity in aquatic environments.
